chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: How long one-nighter and club jobs lasted
summary: Promoters wanted five-hour dances, with a big band playing two and a half hours then a break; club jobs differed.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Uh-huh. I think we may have touched on this, but I can't remember for sure. On your one nighters how often -- or how long were those jobs usually, like from 9:00 to 1:00, 9:00 to 2:00?

I think the majority of the places that we played, the promoters wanted a five hour job, you know, and you wouldn't play like we play now, you know. You play 40 minutes and off 20, like you're supposed to. I don't do that. I play longer, it all depends, and all those things. But in those days, you know, with a big band, you'd play two hours and a half and take a half hour break, you know, and then you go back and you finish the night, you know. This was all you would get. See, so this is what used to happen.
How about in the clubs, was it usually five hours also?

I don't recall too much about it because we didn't play many clubs, Tom, back in those days -- they were little one nighters. Now and then we might play a week stand. I did play a place in Atlanta, Georgia, club, and I think it was like 9:00 to 1:30, and they would actually have to stop
